is_anopheles.evidence: A total of 1397 females... were morphologically identified as belonging to the An. gambiae complex... A subsample of 400 An. gambiae s.l. specimens including 280 control and 120 survivors from bioassays were all found to be An. coluzzii species. (Page 1)

reports_target_markers.evidence: Survivors were genotyped for kdr L1014 mutations using Hot Oligonucleotide Ligation Assay... Among the 120 survivors that were submitted to kdr 1014 genotyping, the kdr 1014 F allele was found at 88 % and 75 % allelic frequencies in survivors from Youpwe and Manoka, respectively (Table 3). None of the analyzed specimens carried the kdr 1014S allele. (Page 1, Page 7-8)

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on page 8 provides kdr L1014 allelic frequencies for survivor An. coluzzii from Manoka (N=44; 75% 1014F, 25% 1014L, 0% 1014S) and Youpwe (N=76; 88% 1014F, 12% 1014L, 0% 1014S). Figure 4 on page 8 reports genotypic frequencies (1014L/1014L, 1014L/1014F, 1014F/1014F) for both populations.

african_field_population.evidence: Anopheline larvae and pupae were collected from open water bodies in December 2013 and April 2014 and reared until adult emergence in the Manoka rural island area compared with the Youpwe suburban inland area, Douala, Cameroon. (Page 1, Page 4)

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field and laboratory study reporting original mosquito collections, bioassay results, species identification, and kdr marker genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: Table 1 on page 6 provides specific geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) for individual larval breeding sites in Manoka (MB1-MB8) and Youpwe (YB1-YB8), Douala, Cameroon.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Larval collections were conducted during two field visits: December 2013 (dry season) and April 2014 (rainy season). (Page 4)

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new primary field collections conducted in December 2013 and April 2014.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype, phenotype, site location, and sample size data are fully presented in the main text, Table 1, Table 3, and Figure 4.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated larval breeding habitats, insecticide resistance, and kdr L1014 (L995) mutations in Anopheles coluzzii populations from Manoka island and Youpwe quarter (Douala, Cameroon) collected in December 2013 and April 2014. Standard WHO susceptibility tests were performed for DDT, permethrin, and deltamethrin with or without PBO. A total of 120 bioassay survivors (44 from Manoka, 76 from Youpwe) were genotyped at the kdr L1014 locus using HOLA. High frequencies of the L1014F (L995F) mutation were observed in survivors from both sites (75% in Manoka, 88% in Youpwe), while the L1014S (L995S) mutation was not detected.
